title: Can LLMs Write Fast Multi-GPU Kernels? — Simran Arora, Together AI
talk_summary: Together AI researchers built a small set of hand-derived primitives (ParallelKittens) for multi-GPU kernels, then benchmarked frontier LLMs on generating such kernels (ParallelKernelBench, 87 problems). Models compile kernels but fail to reason about the underlying trade-offs (transfer mechanism, intra- vs inter-SM scheduling), and gains plateau with more sampling or agentic retries.

takeaways.technique: Capability benchmark with correctness + performance thresholds
takeaways.what_they_do: They score models on two metrics: pass@K (correctness) and fast@K (correct AND beating a reference baseline), and sweep the speedup threshold to see where models fall off.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we measured two main metrics. Um pass at K which is the number of correct kernels generated after K attempts and then fast um one at K
takeaways.numbers: Best frontier model: 28/87 correct zero-shot, 22 faster than baseline; test-time scaling to 36 correct but fast@K plateaus ~31%

takeaways.what_they_do: They found models could get code to compile via retries/self-correction, but still failed on the substantive trade-offs; correctness != quality.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it can often compile the kernels. But the models really struggle to reason through the tradeoffs

takeaways.technique: Provide distilled principles in-context, but expect limited reasoning
takeaways.what_they_do: They gave models the small set of governing trade-off principles in context and still found models did not reason through them, defaulting to patterns seen on the internet.
takeaways.evidence_quote: models do not currently understand how to reason through these trade-offs even when we provide them in context

takeaways.technique: Agentic retry harness has diminishing returns
takeaways.what_they_do: They wrapped a strong model in a mini-SWE-agent multi-turn harness with a local bash env (Claude-Code-like); it improved results but plateaued as time scaled.
takeaways.numbers: 24 -> 35 of 87 solved with agentic harness; 26 above 1x speedup

takeaways.technique: Hand-built primitives beat generic libraries for the hard cases
takeaways.what_they_do: Rather than throwing an LLM at the problem, they first hand-derived minimal primitives and templates, which reached SOTA and are used in production.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we spent the time to build out parallel kittens which is a small set of minimal primitives and patterns
takeaways.numbers: Naive PyTorch+nccl baselines fall below 50% of communication-aware roofline on majority of problems
